When re-evaluated 3 months later, the patient remained stiff in all four limbs, but was nonetheless able to walk. EMG demonstrated continuous motor unit activity in the left biceps brachialis and right triceps surae muscles (Fig. 2). The patient also presented with persistent and severe bladder involvement requiring suprapubic catheter implantation. An oral steroid course was initiated and, 2 months later, anti-GlyR antibodies were positive in both blood and CSF which, in association with the slow gradual evolution, led to initiation of monthly IV cyclophosphamide treatment. At the same time, botulinum toxin injections were given bilaterally in both hypertonic biceps brachialis and triceps surae muscles. Diazepam and baclofen were also started, and resulted in mild improvement of both stiffness and spasm.
